messages:
maria: FYI starting EU failover, eu-west-1 reporting GPU capacity degradation, shifting traffic to eu-west-2. Initiating DNS-based failover now. :rotating_light:

jonas: saw queue length spike ~5m ago, good call. what's the TTL on the A record?

maria: TTL was 3600. lowering to 30 on authoritative now — pushing change, should hit authoritative within 30s.

kevin: lowering helps only for new resolver lookups. lots of corporate/home resolvers will keep the old 1h entry. can we BGP-steer or do an edge-level routing change instead? :thinking: 

maria: traffic-manager BGP steer is an option but we wanted DNS-first to avoid big BGP churn. starting traffic-manager canary to eu-west-2 in parallel.

olivia: fyi some CDNs and enterprise resolvers ignore very low TTLs or clamp them. I'm seeing many client IPs still resolving to eu-west-1 (93.184.216.34) in the access logs.

sre-oncall: action plan: 1) lower authoritative TTL 2) start traffic-manager canary 3) consider temporary more-specific BGP announce if traffic doesn't move. executing 1+2 now.

infra-bot: traffic-manager canary started -> 5% traffic to eu-west-2 (policy id tm-42)

maria: can folks run quick checks from different networks and paste dig results?

jonas: from my corp laptop -> `dig +short A api.redwood.ai @8.8.8.8` returns `93.184.216.34` (still eu-west-1).

kevin: from home ISP -> still old A. contacting NOC to prepare a /24 announce for eu-west-2 as emergency fallback.

olivia: temporary /24 will work fast but be careful: we may affect more prefixes than intended. prefer edge NAT/routing if possible.

maria: starting /24 announce now as emergency measure (only if canary doesn't reduce pressure in 5m).

incident-bot: Incident created: #INC-2026-345 – eu-west-1 GPU pressure + partial DNS failover (created by maria)

incident-bot: BGP action queued: announce 203.0.113.0/24 for eu-west-2 at 2059876610

kevin: BGP announced. watching telemetry — expect flows to move within a couple minutes once upstreams accept the more specific.

jonas: after BGP announce, seeing flow shift in ~90s. 503 overcapacity errors dropped from ~70% -> ~30% in the spiky endpoints.

olivia: still seeing a tail of requests from large corporate resolvers that respect old cache. those will expire as TTLs hit, but could be minutes -> hours depending on resolver.

sre-oncall: estimating full shift in 10-45 minutes due to resolver holdovers. keep BGP /24 until <5% traffic on eu-west-1 or until aux capacity up.

kevin: post-incident recommendations: 1) default service TTL = 60s for public records that are used in failover 2) add monitoring metric 'stale-resolver-rate' (percentage of requests hitting old-region IP) 3) document resolver priming steps in runbook.

maria: agreed. also add a runbook decision matrix: if TTL > 300s then prefer capacity-first (BGP/edge) vs DNS-first.

kevin: i'll create the ticket for TTL tuning and follow-ups. will include rollout plan for edge zones and coordination with NOC.

maria: thanks all. holding BGP announce until we confirm <5% to eu-west-1 or until dedicated capacity scaled. will update every 10m.

sre-oncall: noted, tagging @oncall-night for handover in 20m.

(End-thread)
